games.explanation: The market is treating this like two roughly even teams because Cleveland's uniform still says "contender," but San Diego is meaningfully the better roster and it isn't particularly close. Bibee is a fine arm getting sold as more than that, and the Padres happen to run out the exact bats that punish him, with Tatis and Machado doing damage against righties at rates that make a middle-of-the-zone strike expensive. Mize on the other side gets a Cleveland lineup that outside of Ramirez has been closer to Triple-A filler than a threat, and the sim landing on a one-run Padres win at a pick-'em price is the whole tell. Getting the clearly better team at -108 is the kind of math you take without needing a second look.

picks.explanation: Peralta is the kind of pitcher who racks up strikeouts until a lefty bat makes him pay for the walk he just issued, and Baltimore's lineup is built to make him uncomfortable in exactly that way. His splits against left-handed hitters are a full tick worse across the board, with the walk rate creeping past 12%, and Henderson and Holliday are the sort of patient lefties who turn that flaw into free baserunners. Trevor Rogers has quietly been running a sub-.240 wOBA against, which is more than enough to keep this within a run even if the Rays lineup does its usual damage. The market is pricing this like Tampa runs away with it, and the runline just asks Baltimore to lose respectably, which is the one thing they tend to do well against arms like this.
